accuracy.evidence: Checked against NGSS 3-LS3-1 and its clarification (traits inherited from parents; variation of traits in a group of similar organisms; patterns are similarities and differences between parents and offspring and among siblings) and the NC Year 6 statement that offspring vary and are not identical to their parents. Acquired features (a torn ear, a cut tail, a learned trick, a haircut) are correctly not inherited (Lamarckian inheritance of acquired characteristics is rejected). The litter keeps floppy (lop) ears in all six babies of two lop parents, avoiding an unsupported genetics claim, and varies only coat and size. Sunflower data 160, 170, 150, 180, 170, 160, 190, 170, 180, 170 give counts 1, 2, 4, 2, 1: mode 170 cm, spread 150–190 cm, matching m7 and the lab narration. Item corners: p2 n − b ≥ 1, p4 t − s ≥ 20, m4 n − a ≥ 2, m9 g + b.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented primary misconceptions on inheritance (Driver et al., Making Sense of Secondary Science, ch. on inheritance; AAAS Project 2061 misconception list): acquired injuries are passed on (step 2 prediction 'Yes', torn-ear card, tags injury, p3), learned skills are inherited (Knows a trick card, tags learnpass/looks, m2), offspring are identical to parents or to each other (step 3 prediction, tag identical, m3), a baby takes after only one parent (m8), variation means some are 'not really' the same kind or a measuring error (step 4 prediction, tags notsame/error, p5), and traits come from food or choice (step 1 options, tag food).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagtrait is about inheritance and variation itself: it compares a baby's traits with three candidate parent pairs, sorts inherited versus acquired features, generates a litter from fixed parents whose coat and size vary, and builds a bar chart of sunflower heights from one parent plant. flagbaby names animals and their young, flagadapt covers adaptation to habitats and flagalike sorts by features; none uses parent-offspring comparison or variation data. The 6-shingle gate passes against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Choosing pair A or C gives a reason the floppy ears could not come from them, so the learner works out that traits come from parents; dropping the torn-ear card on Inherited bounces it back with 'happened during the rabbit's life'; the litter grows one baby at a time with narration of each coat, so the learner sees floppy ears in every baby but different fur and sizes; measuring each sunflower drops a block in its height bar, so the chart itself shows most at 170 cm with a spread from 150 to 190 cm, the data evidence 3-LS3-1 asks for.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions with tempting wrong options the lab then disproves: floppy ears come from 'eating carrots' or 'chose them' (only the floppy-eared pair fits); babies 'will be born with a torn ear' (the card belongs in Not inherited); six babies 'will look exactly the same' because they share parents (the litter varies); sunflowers from one plant 'will all be exactly the same height' (the bar chart spreads from 150 to 190 cm).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Nine wrong-answer messages that name the slip: learned (learning happens during life), food (food does not change ear shape), learnpass (a trick is learned, each puppy is taught), looks (looking alike is about body features, not skills), identical (litters vary: different fur and sizes), kind (rabbits always have rabbits), notsame and error (same kind still varies), injury (an injury is not passed on) and life (a haircut is not passed on).

readability.evidence: validate_lessons passes: family kid text FK 3.6 (limit 5.5) and adult FK 6.1 (limit 10.5; a first draft at 11.6 was rewritten into shorter sentences). The kid text uses rabbits, sunflower seeds, a torn ear and a learned trick, and defines 'inherited' and 'variation' in one plain sentence each. Lab step text is two short sentences; buttons say what they do (Pair B, Floppy ears: inherited, Have a baby, Measure the next one, 170 cm bar).

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passes (no banned phrases, explanation overlap under 12% with every lesson, including 174 Animals and their babies). Kid paragraphs: same kind and inherited features; variation in a litter; variation in plants and the bar chart; what is not inherited. Adult paragraphs: standard and key words; named common mistakes; the data and environment caveat; what each lab step does.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots on iPhone 13 (390 px) in light and dark themes after Show me on all 6 steps. The first pass drew rabbits about 25 px tall, too small for 8-year-olds, and black rabbits vanished on the dark theme; rabbits are now about twice the size, the litter is two rows of three, and outlines turn light in dark mode. Cards are full-width tap targets of 34 px or more, sorted cards show in each box at 12 px or larger, sunflower taps snap to the nearest unmeasured flower, and the 5 bar buttons wrap two to a row.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button: Pair A/B/C (aria-labels describe each pair's fur and ears), '<card>: inherited' and '<card>: not inherited' for the next card, Have a baby, Measure the next one, and one button per bar; the challenge uses buttons. say() updates the canvas aria-label and visible narration after each choice, drop, birth and measurement, including colours and heights in words. walk.cjs (desktop and iPhone 13) completes all 5 tasks with Show me, shows the challenge, axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) is clean in both themes, no console errors.
